stem: Propagation losses cluster in one zone across several donors. Which hypothesis becomes more important?
choices: Prioritize donor genetics because losses occurring across several donors indicate that some donor lines are more sensitive than others.
Increase the priority of zone-linked environment, handling, sanitation, or workflow factors because the pattern crosses donor identities.
Treat the records as noncomparable because more than one donor is involved in the affected zone.
Adjust the success denominator by excluding visibly damaged cuttings so zone performance can be compared fairly.
rationale: When losses cluster in one propagation zone across multiple donor identities, a shared local factor becomes more plausible. Environment, sanitation, handling, equipment, workflow timing, or localized contamination can affect several donors at once. Donor genetics can still influence susceptibility, but the cross-donor spatial pattern makes a zone-linked explanation a higher-value hypothesis to test first.
